title: Chinese Medical Interpretation: Testing Mandarin and Cantonese AI Accuracy
summary: Learn how to test AI medical interpretation for Mandarin and Cantonese, including language identification, accents, code-switching, medications, numbers, negation, and clinical speech.
body_markdown:
###


No. Mandarin and Cantonese are distinct spoken varieties and are generally not mutually intelligible, so they should be identified and tested separately for clinical interpretation.


###


Usually not for spoken interpretation. A clinical workflow should identify the patient's actual spoken variety, such as Mandarin or Cantonese, whenever possible.


###


Test each separately using real clinical speech, several speakers, accents, code-switching, medication names, numbers, negation, symptoms, and recovery from unclear turns.


###


Patients may use English medication names, acronyms, or medical terms inside Mandarin or Cantonese speech. The interpreter needs to preserve those terms in context.


###


Yes, if the system supports the patient's spoken variety and performs well on realistic clinical speech. Hospitals should test Mandarin and Cantonese separately instead of relying on a broad Chinese-language claim.
